steps: Locate the unit & fit the top standoffs

Plan unit, vent and gas-line locations together, away from high traffic, furniture and draperies, at the Figure 2 & 3 clearances. Install the top standoffs (shipped loose inside) once the unit is on site and in position.

• Plan the unit, vent and gas-line locations together. Possible locations: an existing wall, a corner, a built-in wall or a wall projection (Figure 8). Keep it out of high traffic and away from furniture and draperies, at the Figure 2 & 3 clearances (p. 5).
  • Codes: the current National Fuel Gas Code, ANSI Z223.1 (USA) or CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada), and local codes. Qualified (licensed or trained) personnel only; in Massachusetts, only a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter.
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: where local codes allow after the "first sale". The fireplace must be fastened in place. Install per Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A (USA), CAN/CSA Z240 MH (Canada).
  • Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room. Must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
  • The top standoffs ship loose inside the fireplace. Install them on top of the unit (Figure 7) once it is on site and in position.
Frame & finish

Unit in place and venting installed first. Assemble the supplied steel stud framing kit, attach it to the framing brackets, and sheet the front in non-combustible board 12" above and 5 7/8" to the sides of the framing edges.

The fireplace should be in place and the venting installed before framing. The steel stud framing kit (supplied) must be used unless the fireplace is totally enclosed with non-combustible material.

  1. Top frame: lay out the side studs and center stud on a large flat surface, the side without screw holes facing down. Screw the header stud and the plate stud to the center stud.
  2. Side studs: fasten the inner side studs to the header and plate studs. Attach the outer side studs to the top of the header stud, and at the bottom with the base plates.
  3. Align the frame to the unit's framing brackets and attach it through the access holes in the outer side studs.
  4. Secure the frame to existing framing through the header stud and the base plates.
  5. Install the non-combustible board on the top and sides with drywall screws. The side of the frame without screw holes faces into the room.

The lintel is fixed: move the fireplace itself so the lintel's front face sets its final position, allowing for the facing thickness. The framing brackets give 1 7/8" of adjustment. Facing must not stop the door or screen from opening.

Hearth: not required. The manual suggests a non-combustible hearth no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace; raise the fireplace for anything thicker, or it will interfere with the door frame. Kit parts list: p. 11. The sheet-metal edges are sharp: wear gloves.
Power & wall switch

110 V. AC to the junction box behind the right-side firebox access panel; mount the wall switch and run the supplied 50 ft cable to the interface board (check continuity before walling in); 4 AA in the wall switch battery pack.

1. Place the fireplace in the desired location.
  2. Remove the door (Door Frame Removal, p. 6).
  3. Remove the access panel from the right-hand side of the firebox.
  4. Connect the 110 V. AC supply to the wires inside the junction box (Power In black, 2 Neutral white, Vent Blower blue). They can be reached from inside and outside the box through either of two small access panels.
  5. Attach the wall switch to the framing (50 ft of cable is supplied).
  6. Route the wall switch control cable to the wall switch.
  7. Connect one end to the wall control and the other to the interface board.
  8. Insert the 4 supplied "AA" batteries into the wall switch battery pack.
  9. If not already installed, install the burner using the instructions supplied with the burner kit.
  10. Turn on the gas supply and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  11. Turn on gas and electrical supplies.
  12. Move the center button on the wall control to ON. The igniter sparks; after a short delay the pilot lights, followed by the main burner.

Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before plugging it into the wall switch and IFC module and before it is walled in. Without home automation only the upper cable is used (wall switch to fireplace).
Set NV / PV · home automation

Set the interface board's NV/PV switch for natural or power venting, with power off and backup batteries out whenever you change it. Optional home automation through a dry contact relay and a 0 - 10 volt DC signal.

The NV / PV switch on the interface board is set for the type of evacuating vent system: NV when vented without a power vent, PV with a power vent (follow the power vent kit's instructions).

When switching between NV and PV, turn off the electrical supply to the fireplace and remove the backup batteries so the module resets properly.

Home automation (optional)

  • Flame and light on/off through a dry contact relay; flame and light level from high to low with a 0 - 10 volt DC signal (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts).
  • Two cables: the top one from the wall switch to the fireplace, the bottom one from the wall switch to the home automation system. Wire designations: Figure 32 (p. 18).
  • Leave the wall switch on Remote. The control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command arrives.
  • Basic Wall Switch: flame on and off only, through a dry contact relay on the solid brown wire and common.
Gas supply + leak check

3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet through the control box's top or left access holes; sediment trap within 6 feet of the valve; union or flare fitting, never hard-piped. Check every connection is tight and leak free; refit the access panel and gasket.

• Gas line by a qualified service person, to all building codes.
  • Access holes: top and left sides of the control box. The valve inlet accepts a 3/8" N.P.T. fitting; use the correct gas line diameter.
  • Sediment trap, per the national fuel gas code, no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve.
  • Do not hard pipe the line to the valve: provide a union or flare fitting so the valve can be repaired or replaced.
  • The main gas connection is reached through the back of the control box on the right side of the fireplace; there should be a red plug in the fitting (p. 20).
  • Connect to the gas connector, turn on the gas and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
Supply NG / LP5.0" / 12.5" WC min · 13.9" WC max
Manifold NG3.5" WC max · 1.6" WC min
Manifold LP10" WC max · 6.4" WC min

Verify pressures with the fireplace lit on its highest setting. Turn off the gas before removing a test-port plug. The test procedure is in the Burner Installation Manual.

Refit the access panel and its gasket after installation, conversion or servicing. Without it the control system overheats and fails early.
Vent & terminate

Wall kit 22270012 or roof kit 22270010 only. Screw and tape every joint, slope horizontal runs 1/4" per 1 ft toward the termination, support every 4', and stay inside the Figure 40 / 41 rise-run charts.

Only Town & Country termination kits 22270012 (wall) or 22270010 (roof). Screw every joint and seal it with the high temperature self-adhesive tape provided. Slope horizontal runs 1/4" rise per 1 ft toward the termination; at least 1 support every 4'; combustibles no closer than 1 3/4" to the pipe.

Wall termination

  1. Position the fireplace so the vent is centred (if possible) between framing members. The vent kit handles walls up to 12" thick.
  2. Cut and frame a 14 1/2" opening (round or square), centred at least 52 7/16" above the floor; higher as the horizontal run grows (Figure 40). Keep the terminal clearances (p. 28).
  3. At least 1 foot of pipe off the top before the first elbow; at that rise with a 90° elbow, up to 24 inches of horizontal past the elbow.
  4. Trim the wall thimble to the wall thickness, siding included, and fit it from inside so it is flush with the outer wall.
  5. Run the pipe through the thimble to the flue collar; it must not protrude beyond the outer wall.
  6. Engage the terminal so the inner and outer pipes are fully engaged, attach it to the outside wall (never recessed into the wall or siding) and caulk it.

Roof termination

  1. Cut and frame a 14 1/2" opening in each floor, ceiling or roof; the roof opening grows with pitch to keep a 1 3/4" air space. Avoid cutting rafters.
  2. Fit a ceiling firestop at each floor or ceiling. Into an attic, leave the shield full length and add a storm collar on top (an attic insulation shield, SKU #22270029, may be required).
  3. Run pipe from the collar on top of the fireplace up through the roof: at least 12" above the roof, more on steeper pitches (roof pitch table, p. 28).
  4. Roof support bracket to the roof joists, flashing sealed to the roof, storm collar with a ring of mastic, then the termination cap screwed on and caulked.
Set the vent restrictor
Ships wide open. Read the position for the vent height and horizontal length from Figure 48, loosen the screw, move the restrictor, re-tighten. Fully open with a power vent.

The restrictor is on the underside of the firebox top and leaves the factory wide open. It tunes secondary airflow for flame appearance and performance.

  1. Determine the vent height and the horizontal length.
  2. Find the restrictor position on the chart in Figure 48 (p. 30). It is drawn as a graph; read it from the page.
  3. Loosen the screw holding the restrictor, move it to its intended opening, and re-tighten.

Positions are based on lab tests; the ideal may vary slightly with the installation.

Too closedflame excessively tall and lifting, lacks movement, soots
Too openflame height low, excessive movement
Power vent: the restrictor must be fully open.
Install the firebox panels
Required for safe operation, before the logs and grate: retainer off, rear lower, right side, rear upper, left side, retainers back on, then the left and right front panels.

A firebox panel set must be installed for safe operation; don't use the fireplace without panels. Install them before the logs and grate. Unpack and inspect them: they are very fragile, and fibre panels may need trimming to fit. For porcelain panels, see their own instruction manual first.

  1. Remove the side panel retainer (two screws) from under the firebox heat shield.
  2. Rear lower panel.
  3. Right side panel: bottom in first, then angle it up. You may need to push the firebox shield up.
  4. Rear upper panel.
  5. Left side panel: bottom in first, then angle it up.
  6. Re-install the side panel retainers.
  7. Left and right front panels.

Maker's website: Compatible Firebox Panels: Aspen, Black Porcelain, Coffee Bean Brown Porcelain, Copper Porcelain, Madison, Manhattan, Mount Vernon, Park Avenue, Titanium Porcelain. Install to the manual.
Trim kit & safety barrier
With the door in place: magnetic side trims, then the top trim, then the meshed bottom piece with the T&C badge on its right; attach the magnetic safety barrier screen.

Transition trim kit SKU #80002251: two side pieces, a top piece and a meshed bottom piece, fitted once the door is installed.

  1. With the door in place, set out the two side pieces and the top piece; each takes 2 button magnets (included).
  2. Install the side pieces first, with the two smaller magnets on each.
  3. Install the top piece over the side pieces with the two larger magnets.
  4. Rest the meshed bottom piece on the floor, in the gap between the outer-most door frame and the glass.
  5. Fix the Town & Country badge to the right-hand side of the bottom piece.
  6. Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer-most door frame.
Pair wall switch & remote
Pair the wall switch to the fireplace, then the remote to the wall switch (Basic Wall Switch: the remote pairs to the module). Repeat the first step to change channel if another fireplace responds.

Bluetooth wall switch

  1. Wall switch to fireplace: selector to Remote; hold the Program button (straightened paper clip) for up to 10 seconds; release after 5 beeps. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more.
  2. Wall switch to remote: press and release Program once (3 beeps), then within 60 sec. press and release on/off on the remote. The wall switch beeps 3 times.

Basic wall switch

The remote pairs directly to the module: press and release Program once (3 beeps from the module), then on/off on the remote within 60 sec.; the module beeps 3 times.

If another fireplace nearby responds instead, repeat the wall-switch-to-fireplace step: it moves to another of three available channels. Phone pairing (TC Fire app) is in the owner's manual.

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an ignition device lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace for gas, and next to the floor too. Some gas is heavier than air and settles there. If you smell gas, don't try to light any appliance. Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

To turn it on

  1. Push the On/Off switch to turn the fireplace on. It can take up to 30 seconds to light each time.
  2. If the burner lights, use the hand-held remote to set it the way you want.
  3. If it doesn't light, push the On/Off switch to off. Wait at least 5 minutes for any gas inside the fireplace to clear. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety. If you don't, try step 1 again.
Won't light or stay lit after several tries? Switch it off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace, and call your service technician or gas supplier.
Lighting it for the first time? Allow enough time for air to escape from the gas lines.

To turn it off

Push the On/Off switch to off. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power to it and take out the backup batteries.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. A single beep from the fireplace confirms each command.

On/Off keyturns the fireplace on or off
Up / Down arrow keysflame height, 6 levels
Mode keysteps to the light and pilot settings
Mode + Up togetherkey lock on or off

Flame

Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one step, until it is off. The up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow brings the flame back on high.

Light

Press Mode until the light bulb icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of 6 levels.

Pilot: IPI or CPI

With the system off, press Mode to reach the CPI icon. Up turns on continuous pilot ignition (CPI). Down returns to intermittent pilot ignition (IPI).

Fahrenheit or Celsius

With the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode at the same time, then check for the C or F beside the room temperature.

Thermostat: the thermostat function is off by default. It is not permitted in the USA (it is in Canada).
Remote batteries low or dead? Turn the fireplace off with the on/off switch on the wall switch.

sounds.title: First fire: smells, sounds and beeps
sounds.html:
A smell the first time

The first time you light it, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. It comes from paints, sealants and lubricants from manufacturing as they cure. It is temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room; the odor can bother some people.

Ticking and creaking

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they start up and cool down. Your furnace heat exchanger and cook stove oven make similar noises.

A short wait

It can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you select On.

Beeps

  • One beep from the fireplace: your command was received.
  • A double-beep when it receives a command: the fireplace's backup batteries are low.
A gas smell is different. Don't light any appliance, touch any electrical switch or use any phone in the building. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone, or the fire department if you can't reach them.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, with fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Never clean the glass while it is hot.
  • No abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • Clean the outside finish with mild soap and water.

If the door has to come off

These steps are in the installation manual (p. 6). Turn the fireplace off and let it cool fully first. The ceramic glass is very fragile.

  1. Pry the top of the safety barrier screen toward you and lift it off its tabs at the base of the door frame. Remove the trim kit too, if you have one.
  2. Push a screwdriver against the notch at the top of a latch, grab the bottom of the latch handle as it sticks out, and lift until the hook lets go. Repeat on the other side, holding the glass so it can't tip out.
  3. Tilt the top of the frame out, then lift it up and out of its bottom track.

Put it back in reverse order: each latch handle should snap in flush with the frame. Then refit the trim and the safety screen.

Cracked or broken glass? Don't use the fireplace until it is replaced, by a licensed or qualified service person, with ceramic glass only.

app.title: Wall switch, pairing and the TC Fire app
app.html:
The fireplace is linked to the wall switch first, then the wall switch to the remote.

1 · Wall switch to fireplace

  1. Set the wall switch selector to Remote.
  2. With a straightened paper clip, press and hold the wall switch's Program button for up to 10 seconds.
  3. Let go after the wall switch beeps 5 times. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more: they're linked.

2 · Remote to wall switch

  1. Press and release the Program button once. The wall switch beeps 3 times.
  2. Within 60 seconds, press and release On/Off on the remote. The wall switch beeps 3 times: it's linked.
A nearby fireplace turns on instead? Repeat part 1. It moves to another of three channels.

TC Fire app (Bluetooth)

Get the free TC Fire app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Open Add/Edit Fireplace, press Add, enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch and a name for the fireplace, then press Save. The app turns the flame and the light on and off and sets their levels. You'll only see the fireplace when your phone is in Bluetooth range and no one else is controlling it.

power.title: Batteries and power outages
power.html:
The fireplace's control runs on household power, with a battery pack as backup.

Remote3 AAA batteries
Backup pack, in the wall switch4 AA batteries

The backup batteries are used only when line power is interrupted or lost, and only if the fireplace does not use a combustion fan.

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen before the power runs out, and goes away when you replace the batteries.
  • Backup batteries: the fireplace gives a double-beep when it receives a command. With fresh batteries it beeps once when you press a key.

Battery life depends on battery quality, how often the fireplace lights, and similar things.

Turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace before you remove or put back the batteries.
For service or a long shutdown, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and remove the backup batteries.

bulb.title: Replacing the light bulb
bulb.html:
Before any servicing, turn off the gas and electrical power and give the fireplace plenty of time to cool.

Take out the old bulb

  1. Remove the screw that holds the light cover in the upper heat shield at the top of the firebox, then pull the light assembly down slightly.
  2. Slip a small flat screwdriver between the glass lens and the light box, and twist carefully to pop the lens open.
  3. Pull the old bulb away from the plug end, wiggling it gently.

Put in the new bulb

  1. Hold the new bulb with a paper towel or cloth. Don't touch it with your fingers: skin oils can make it fail early. If you do touch it, clean it with alcohol before use.
  2. Push it into the plug end, wiggling it gently.
  3. Push the glass lens up to close it.
  4. Fit the plug end of the light assembly back into the light box and secure it with the single screw you removed.

The installation manual's parts list gives the replacement as halogen light bulb 80002650 (p. 42).

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Hot glass

The glass gets hot enough to burn. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The fireplace comes with a barrier that reduces the risk of burns from the hot glass. It must be installed to protect children and others at risk.

Around the fireplace

  • Supervise young children in the same room. A safety gate can keep toddlers away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies, gasoline and other flammable liquids and vapors away.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician immediately to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Don't run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or with any panel or door left off after service.
This is a decorative fireplace. The installation manual says it is not intended to be used as a heating appliance.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting at least once a year. The manual also asks for an inspection before use. Lots of lint from carpeting, bedding and the like can mean more frequent cleaning.

What the annual inspection covers

  • Remove the glass and check the decorative media (logs, pebbles, glass and so on) for soot. With excessive soot, a qualified service person should inspect and adjust the unit for proper combustion.
  • Clean the media, and brush or vacuum the burner, paying close attention to the burner ports.
  • Check the pilot for proper flame size and operation, and clean off soot, dust or other deposits.
  • Check that the vent pipe and vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  • Check the glass gasket and replace it if needed. A good glass seal matters.
  • Check and replace batteries as needed.

Control compartments, burners and air passageways must be kept clean, and the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials, gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

Before any service, turn off the gas and electrical power and let the fireplace cool.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
The Town & Country limited lifetime warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only)limited lifetime, parts only
Combustion chamberlimited lifetime, parts only
Burner tube assemblylimited lifetime, parts only
Porcelain finisheslimited lifetime, parts only
Any defective part2 years, parts and labor, from the original purchase date

Conditions

  • Installed by a qualified technician, to local and national requirements and the appliance manual.
  • Sediment trap within 6 feet of the gas control valve.
  • The installer makes sure it fires as per the rating plate.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors may darken when heated and return to the original shade when cool.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Installation, operating or environmental conditions beyond Town & Country's control.
Not following the manual's installation or operating instructions voids the warranty. This is a summary; the full terms are in the PDF.

The rating label gives mantel to appliance 9 in. (229 mm) and maximum mantel extension 12 in. (305 mm), and refers to the installation manual for more detail. The mantel clearance chart there (Figure 2, p. 5) is a lettered diagram: read its clearance and depth combinations from the page.

The top standoffs ship loose inside the fireplace and must be installed on top of it. Keep combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier and gas plumbing out of the non-combustible zone within the steel stud framing.

specFraming.title: Framing, facing & hearth
specFraming.html:
Framing

  • Fireplace in place and venting installed before framing.
  • The supplied Steel Stud Framing Kit (80001063) must be used unless the fireplace is totally enclosed with non-combustible material. Attach it to the framing brackets on each side once the unit is in its final position.
  • Sides, back and top may be framed with conventional lumber up to the steel studs and the standoffs; set studs back for the finish thickness.
  • Minimum combustible framing dimensions are drawn in Figures 10 and 11 (p. 9).

Front sheeting

  • Non-combustible backer board (cement board or equivalent) on the front, extending 12" above and 5 7/8" to the side of the framing edge bars; standard drywall beyond.
  • Wall above to be painted: discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board (1/2" thick) or equivalent with full length metal studs. Pre-drilling the board is recommended.

Lintel and facing

  • Fixed lintel: position the fireplace so the lintel's front face sets its final position. The framing brackets give 1 7/8" of adjustment.
  • Flush finish: facing up to 1 7/8" thick (p. 14). Page 8 notes a thickness of 3/4" finishes flush with the front of the unit.
  • Finishing material must not stop the door or screen from opening: the door must be able to open in the event of ignition of excess gas buildup.
Note: p. 5 says the unit may be recessed up to 4 1/2" with non-combustible masonry type material, and p. 14 says it can be installed with a 4 1/2 inch recess (p. 10 allows a deeper recess with the facing moved away from the face of the unit and the window, top and sides, at a ratio of 1:1, up to a maximum 12" deep); p. 8 says additional masonry type non-combustible material can be installed above and to the sides up to 6 inches proud of the appliance.

Hearth and chase

  • No hearth extension is required, but a non-combustible hearth no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace is suggested. Raise the fireplace for anything thicker: thicker hearths interfere with the door frame.
  • Exterior chase: insulating the outer walls to the same degree as other exterior walls is recommended; cover the insulation and plastic vapour barrier with a solid surface such as drywall, and don't place the fireplace directly against insulation. No insulation or plastic vapour barrier within the framing kit. Seal the chase at the ceiling level or between floors.

With the minimum 1 foot rise and a 90° elbow, up to 24 inches of horizontal is allowed past the elbow; longer runs need more rise. Rise and run must stay inside the chart. The tables pair each minimum rise with a maximum run (all approximate): wall, Figure 40 (p. 24), from 52 7/16" rise / 34 5/16" run to 87 11/16" rise / 250 5/16" run; roof, Figure 41 (p. 25), from 52 7/16" / 41" to 87 11/16" / 250". Keep the vent short with few elbows for best performance and flame appearance.

Join every component tightly with sheet metal screws and seal with the high temperature self-adhesive tape provided. Optional power vents (22270003, 22270004 and 22270013) have different venting requirements: see the power vent manual.

  • The gas control system is on the right-hand side of the firebox behind an access panel (and the decorative firebox panel, if installed). The junction box wires can be reached from inside or outside through either of two small access panels.
  • Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before plugging it into the wall switch and the IFC module, and before walling it in.
  • NV / PV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one. When switching, turn off the electrical supply and remove the backup batteries to reset the module.
  • Home automation: a dry contact relay switches flame and light on/off; a 0 - 10 volt DC signal sets their level (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts). Leave the wall switch on Remote. Basic Wall Switch: flame on/off only, on the solid brown wire and common.

review.notes: Page numbers are physical PDF pages; owner topics link to the Owner's (operator) manual, installer topics to the Installation Manual. Ignition is Proflame 2 electronic (IFC module, automatic pilot ignition) with IPI/CPI selectable on the remote; the lighting label (doc 2 p. 4) says never light the pilot by hand. Diagram-only content not transcribed (said to be on the page instead): fireplace dimensions (Figure 1, p. 5, unlabelled); the mantel clearance chart (Figure 2, p. 5: clearances 9"/6"/3" and depths 12"/6 3/4"/1 1/2", pairing only in the drawing; the guide quotes the rating label's 9 in. mantel to appliance / 12 in. maximum extension, p. 43); framing kit and minimum combustible framing dimensions (Figures 9-11, p. 8-9); main gas connection dimensions (Figure 34, p. 20); the rise/run graphs (Figures 40-41); roof opening sizes by pitch (A/B table with Figure 42, p. 26); roof clearance drawing values (Figure 45, p. 28); vent restrictor positions (Figure 48, p. 30, including its 1" OPEN NG / 3/4" OPEN LP labels); vent pipe dimensions and offset charts (p. 32-33); wiring diagram (p. 40). The wall venting table's 4th row reads 1 x 24"+ 1 x 8" and 4 x48" + 1 x 4" (p. 24), lengths not in the Figure 38 component list, while the roof table's 4th row reads 1 x 24" + 1 x 18" and 4 x 48" + 1 x 24" (p. 25); the guide quotes only the first and last rows of each table. Not covered by these manuals, so left out: burner, log/media and light-kit installation and the gas pressure test procedure (separate burner kit / Burner Installation Manual); any fuel conversion kit (the manual only says 'unless a certified kit is used'); power vent installation (separate power vent manual); fan/blower operation (doc 2 p. 7 describes the Proflame 2's six-speed comfort fan generically, the rating label gives a blower rating, but there are no TC30 fan instructions). No troubleshooting chart and no LED/code table: fault panels are built from the vent restrictor flame descriptions (p. 30), the lighting instructions (doc 2 p. 4) and the control notes (doc 2 p. 6, 8, 10-11); codes left empty and beeps covered in the drawers. Thermostat: doc 2 p. 6 says it is disabled by default and not permissible in the USA; the Canadian enabling procedure (doc 2 p. 9) is not reproduced. The owner glass drawer uses the installation manual's Door Frame Removal steps (doc 1 p. 6). Facing thickness is shown both ways and not flagged as a conflict: p. 8 says 3/4" finishes flush with the front of the unit, p. 14 says facing up to 1 7/8" can be accommodated if installing flush (framing bracket range 1 7/8", p. 13). Backup batteries: the installation manual puts the 4 AA in the wall switch battery pack (p. 15); the owner's manual calls them the IFC module's backup batteries (doc 2 p. 7, 10). Manual cross-reference slips: linking instructions said to be on 'page 36 / 37' (printed pages 37-38; doc 1 p. 16); maintenance points to the VENTING section 'Page 20' (venting starts on p. 21; doc 1 p. 39); the light-bulb step cites Figure 25 instead of Figure 33 (doc 2 p. 18). The rating label gives manifold maximums only; the minimums come from the p. 19 table. Model naming varies: TC30D2 / MODEL TC30 SERIES D2 (install cover), MODEL TC30 SERIES D - Version 2 (owner cover), SERIES D (rating label). Catalog items the manuals can't confirm: view area 691 sq in; power venting 'up to 110 ft from an exterior wall'; 'electronic ignition that can be switched to standing pilot' (the manuals call it CPI, continuous pilot ignition); 'battery backup keeps it running in a power outage' (doc 2 p. 7 limits battery use to when line power is lost and the fireplace does not use a combustion fan). Catalog efficiency 34.5% (P.4.1) and its clearances note (A 9 / B 6 / C 3 in, depths 12 / 6-3/4 / 1-1/2 in, side wall 4 in, ceiling 24 in, vent 1-3/4 in) match p. 5 and p. 43.
